Denis-Ryan, A., Bataille, C. and Jotzo, F. (2016). Managing carbon-intensive materials in a decarbonizing world without a global price on carbon. Climate Policy 16(sup1), S110-S128. Supplemental material (Technical appendices; file tcpo_a_1176008_sm9049.docx). doi:10.1080/14693062.2016.1176008

Word file with no page numbers; locators are the appendix table numbers. The three tables are EMF images, not Word tables: text was read from the EMF text records with python and checked against a LibreOffice render of Table 2. Table 2 (iron and steel, per t crude steel, global; 2012 average / best performance / BAT / new technologies) loaded: direct fuel and electricity use (GJ/t), direct CO2 without CCS, share captured and derived captured CO2 for the CCS routes. Routes are whole routes (BF-BOF, DRI-EAF, scrap EAF) excluding casting and rolling, which is a separate row. Fuel and electricity emission factors, indirect and with-CCS totals go to other-values. Table 3 (cement; 2012 global average / IEA-based 2050 / literature low range): clinker thermal energy, process, energy and direct emissions per t clinker loaded; cement-level ratios, fuel factors and electricity to other-values. NO COSTS: the supplement holds no capital or operating costs, so any cost assumptions Bataille 2017 attributes to it are not here. Table 1 (material-efficiency shares) is an image of sector percentages and was not loaded. Every number is reprinted from the literature cited in the table rows (Birat 2010, Carbon Trust 2011, Worrell et al. 2007, IEA 2009-2015, Fischedick et al. 2014, etc.). TRAPS: cement 'Electricity use' prints 0.80 MWh/t cement in the 2050 and low columns versus 0.096 for 2012 (likely 0.080), not loaded; direct emissions in the 2050 and low cement columns are net of the CCS share while process and energy emissions are before capture; technology names steel-mill_* and rolling-mill_casting-and-rolling are composed route names (steel-mill is not in the equipment vocabulary). Heating-value basis not stated.
